newsitem.title: USA: U.S. steel imports jump 64 pct in August - report.
newsitem.headline: U.S. steel imports jump 64 pct in August - report.

text.p: U.S. August steel imports jumped 63.4 percent to 2.96 million net tons from August 1995, for the highest monthly total since January 1995, the American Iron and Steel Institute said Friday.
In a report based on U.S. Commerce Department data, it said August imports were up 13.9 pecent from July's level.
Imports in the first eight months of the year totaled 17.98 million tons, 0.6 percent up on the same year-earlier period, it said.

August imports accounted for 27 percent of apparent consumption, up from 18.8 percent a year earlier and 25.2 percent in July. Year-to-date imports represent 22.0 percent of consumption, down from 22.6 percent a year earlier.
Net exports in August of 383,888 tons were down 46.3 percent from August 1995 but were up 1.2 percent from July 1996, while year-to-date 3.51 million tons, off 14.2 percent.
Main countries of origin for imports were the European Union (918,000 tons), Brazil (410,000) and Canada (402,000).
